evidence.description: The tabManager property is declared without any synchronization.
The setTabManager method modifies the property without synchronization.
The closeTab method accesses tabManager without synchronization.

candidates.explanation: The `tabManager` property is accessed and modified from multiple threads (via `observerQueue` and `DispatchQueue.main`) without any synchronization mechanism, which can lead to race conditions.
candidates.title: Potential Race Condition on TabManager Property

evidence.description: Observers are added on the main queue.
Cleanup and management occur on a concurrent queue with barriers.

candidates.explanation: The code adds observers on the `.main` queue (lines 120, 155) but performs cleanup and management on a concurrent `observerQueue` with barriers. While the barrier ensures thread-safe access to the dictionary, the interaction between the main queue's execution and the concurrent queue's management of those observers can lead to complex timing issues.
candidates.title: Inconsistent Threading for Notification Center Observers

evidence.description: Suffixing keys to distinguish observer types.
Filtering keys by substring to count tracked tabs.

candidates.explanation: The code uses string concatenation and substring filtering (e.g., "_pageload") to distinguish between different types of observers stored in the same dictionary. This is error-prone and less efficient than using a nested dictionary or a dedicated struct to group observers by tab UUID.
candidates.title: Redundant String Manipulation for Key Tracking
